questions.question: ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral such that AB is a diameter of the circle circumscribing it and ∠ADC = 118°. What is the measure of ∠BAC?
questions.solution:
**Given: **

AB is a diameter.

ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral in which ∠ADC = 118°

**Concept used:**

The angle formed by the diameter of the circle at the circumference of the circle is always 90° 

ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral 

So, ∠ADC + ∠ABC = 180° 

**Calculation: **

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5126e1757bbd676c6b981c5972ddcea895ec17995ff3ce00051eb653524474a1.png] **

In a cyclic quadrilateral, the sum of each pair of opposite angles is 180 degrees.

⇒ ∠ADC + ∠ABC = 180°

⇒ 118° + ∠ABC = 180°

⇒ ∠ABC = 62°

∠ACB = 90° ----(The angle formed by the diameter of the circle at the circumference of the circle always 90°)

In ΔABC,

∠BAC + ∠ACB + ∠ABC = 180°

⇒ ∠BAC + 90° + 62° = 180°

⇒ ∠BAC = 28°

**∴ The value of ∠BAC is 28° **

questions.question: PQRS is a cyclic quadrilateral and PQ is a diameter of the circle. If ∠RPQ = 23°, then what is the measure of ∠PSR?
questions.solution:
Given:

PQRS is a cyclic quadrilateral and PQ is the diameter of the circle. 

∠RPQ = 23°

Concept used:

In the case of a cyclic quadrilateral, the sum of opposite angles of the quadrilateral is 180°.

The sum of all internal angles of a triangle is 180°.

The angle subtended by a diameter on any point of a circle is 90°.

Calculation:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6b7829eed107f7fa2f0fc7fc931337168a2b25f09a12992165fff21b95d1a168.png] 

According to the concept, ∠PRQ = 90°

Considering ΔPRQ,

∠RPQ + ∠RQP + ∠PRQ = 180°

⇒ 23° + ∠RQP + 90° = 180°

⇒ ∠RQP = 180° - 113°

⇒ ∠RQP = 67°

Since the circle is circumscribed on a quadrilateral PQRS, PQRS is a cyclic quadrilateral.

So, ∠RQP + ∠PSR = 180°

⇒ 67° + ∠PSR = 180°

⇒ ∠PSR = 180° - 67°

⇒ ∠PSR = 113°

**∴ The measure of ∠PSR is 113°.**

questions.question: One side of a rhombus is 6.5 cm and one of its’s diagonal is 12 cm. What is the area of the rhombus?
questions.solution:

a² = (d₁/2)² + (d₂/2)²

6.5² = (12/2)² + (d₂/2)²

42.25 = 6² + (d₂/2)²

questions.question: In a quadrilateral ABCD, the bisectors of ∠C and ∠D meet at point E. If ∠CED = 57° and ∠A = 47°, then the measure of ∠B is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

∠CED = 57° and ∠A = 47°

**Concept used:**

The sum of the all angles of a triangle = 180°

The sum of the all angles of a quadrilateral = 360°

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/30c0f85882aa49c6023fd21a7713b9da51260db1254e1dced67f52eace08da42.png] 

In ΔCED, ∠CDE + ∠DCE + ∠CED = 180°

⇒ ∠D/2 + ∠C/2 + 57° = 180°

⇒ ∠D/2 + ∠C/2 = 180° - 57° = 123°

⇒ (∠D + ∠C)/2 = 123°

⇒ ∠D + ∠C = 123° × 2 = 246°

Also, ∠A + ∠B + ∠C + ∠D = 360°

⇒ 47° + ∠B + 246° = 360° [∵ ∠D + ∠C = 246°]

⇒ ∠B = 360° - 246° - 47° = 67°

**∴ The measure of ∠B is 67°**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__** ∠CED = 57° and ∠A = 47°

The bisectors of *∠C* and *∠D *meet at point E

∠A + ∠B = 2 ∠CED

⇒ 47° + ∠B = 2 × 57°

⇒ ∠B = 114° - 47° = 67°

∴ The measure of ∠B is 67°

questions.question: The side MN of a parallelogram MNOP is produced to Q such that MN = NQ. PQ intersects ON at R. The point R divides ON in the ratio:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In parallelogram MNOP, opposite side OP is parallel and equal to MN.

Line MN is extended to Q such that MN = NQ, making OP parallel and equal to NQ.

The intersection of PQ and ON at R forms two triangles: ΔPOR and ΔQNR.

Since OP || NQ, alternate interior angles are equal, and with OP = NQ, ΔPOR ≅ ΔQNR (ASA congruence).

Therefore, corresponding sides OR and RN are equal, meaning R is the midpoint of ON.

**∴ The correct answer is 1 : 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

MNOP is a parallelogram.

MN is produced to Q such that MN = NQ.

PQ intersects ON at R.

**Formula Used:**

Properties of parallelograms and congruent triangles (ASA criterion).

 

 

 

 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 M
 N
 Q
 O
 P
 R
 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 

 

 

**Calculations:**

⇒ In parallelogram MNOP, opposite sides are parallel and equal, so OP || MN and OP = MN.

⇒ Line MN is produced to Q, so OP || NQ.

⇒ It is given that MN = NQ. Thus, substituting MN, we get OP = NQ.

⇒ In ΔPOR and ΔQNR:

⇒ ∠POR = ∠QNR (Alternate interior angles, as OP || NQ and ON is the transversal)

⇒ ∠OPR = ∠NQR (Alternate interior angles, as OP || NQ and PQ is the transversal)

⇒ OP = NQ (Proved above)

⇒ By ASA congruence criterion, ΔPOR ≅ ΔQNR.

⇒ Since corresponding parts of congruent triangles are equal, OR = RN.

⇒ This implies R is the midpoint of ON, so it divides ON in the ratio 1 : 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 1 : 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Congruence of Triangles (ASA Rule)

Two triangles are congruent if two angles and the included side of one are equal to the corresponding parts of the other. Congruent triangles have equal corresponding side lengths.

Properties of a Parallelogram

In a parallelogram, opposite sides are strictly parallel and equal in length. The opposite angles are equal, and the diagonals bisect each other perfectly.

Alternate Interior Angles

When a transversal line intersects two parallel lines, the alternate interior angles formed on opposite sides of the transversal line are equal.
</p

questions.question: PQRS is a cyclic quadrilateral with QR as the diameter of the circle. If ∠SQR = 24°, then what will be the measure of ∠QPS?
questions.solution:

∠SQR = 24°

⇒ 24° + 90° + ∠QRS = 180° 

⇒ 114° + ∠QRS = 180° 

⇒ ∠QRS = (180° – 114°)

⇒ ∠QRS = 66° 

Now,

∠QPS + ∠QRS = 180° [sum of pair of opposite sides of cyclic quadrilateral is 180°]

⇒ ∠QPS + 66° = 180° 

⇒ ∠QPS = (180° – 66°)

⇒ ∠QPS = 114° 

**∴ The required value of ∠QPS is 114° **

questions.question: A quadrilateral PQRS is inscribed in a circle of centre O, such that PQ is a diameter and ∠ PSR = 120°. Find the value of ∠QPR.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a cyclic quadrilateral, opposite angles sum to 180°.

⇒ ∠PQR = 180° − ∠PSR = 180° − 120° = 60°

The angle subtended by a diameter at the circumference is always 90°.

⇒ ∠PRQ = 90°

In right-angled ΔPQR, ∠QPR = 180° − (90° + 60°) = 30°

**∴ The correct answer is 30°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

PQ is the diameter of the circle with centre O.

PQRS is a cyclic quadrilateral inscribed in the circle.

∠PSR = 120°

 ∴ ∠QPR = 30°

**Formula Used:**

1. The sum of opposite angles in a cyclic quadrilateral is 180°.

2. The angle subtended by a diameter at the circumference of a circle is 90°.

3. The sum of interior angles of a triangle is 180°.

**Calculation:**

Since PQRS is a cyclic quadrilateral, the sum of its opposite angles is 180°.

⇒ ∠PSR + ∠PQR = 180°

⇒ 120° + ∠PQR = 180°

⇒ ∠PQR = 180° − 120° = 60°

Since PQ is the diameter, the angle formed in the semicircle is a right angle.

⇒ ∠PRQ = 90°

Now, consider ΔPQR. The sum of all angles in a triangle is 180°.

⇒ ∠QPR + ∠PQR + ∠PRQ = 180°

⇒ ∠QPR + 60° + 90° = 180°

⇒ ∠QPR + 150° = 180°

⇒ ∠QPR = 180° − 150° = 30°

**∴ The correct answer is 30°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cyclic Quadrilateral Property

A quadrilateral whose all four vertices lie on a circle is called a cyclic quadrilateral. The sum of either pair of opposite angles is exactly 180° (∠A + ∠C = 180° and ∠B + ∠D = 180°).

Angle in a Semicircle

According to Thales's Theorem, any angle subtended by a diameter of a circle at any point on the circumference is always a right angle (90°).

Angle Subtended by an Arc

The angle subtended by an arc at the centre is double the angle subtended by it at any remaining part of the circle.
</p

questions.question: ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral. AB and DC meet at F, when produced. AD and BC meet at E, when produced. If ∠BAD = 68° and ∠AEB = 27°, then what is the measure of ∠BFC?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral

∠BAD = 68° 

∠AEB = 27°

**Concept used:**

Sum of opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral is 180° 

Sum of linear pair of angles of is always 180° 

Sum of all 3 interior angles of triangle is 180° 

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e8e02feb49d138d991a32e22c9a519f89206f9c40185abf03fb2339951c47caa.png] 

∠BAE + ∠BEA + ∠ABE = 180° 

⇒ 68° + 27° + ∠ABE = 180° 

⇒ 95° + ∠ABE = 180° 

⇒ ∠ABE = (180° – 95°)

⇒ ∠ABE = 85° 

Now,

∠ABE + ∠CBF = 180° [linear pair]

⇒ 85° + ∠CBF = 180° 

⇒ ∠CBF = (180° – 85°)

⇒ ∠CBF = 95° 

Now,

∠BAE + ∠BCD = 180° [opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral]

⇒ 68° + ∠BCD = 180° 

⇒ ∠BCD = (180° – 68°)

⇒ ∠BCD = 112° 

Now,

∠BCD + ∠BCF = 180° [linear pair]

⇒ 112° + ∠BCF = 180° 

⇒ ∠BCF = (180° – 112°)

⇒ ∠BCF = 68° 

Now,

In ΔBCF

∠BCF + ∠CBF + ∠BFC = 180° 

⇒ 68° + 95° + ∠BFC = 180° 

⇒ 163° + ∠BFC = 180° 

⇒ ∠BFC = (180° – 163°)

⇒ ∠BFC = 17° 

**∴ The required value is 17° **

∠BCD

questions.question: In a rhombus ABCD, O is any interior point such that OA = OC. What is five-ninths of the degree measure of ∠DOB?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

In a rhombus, diagonals act as perpendicular bisectors for each other.

Any point equidistant from vertices A and C (OA = OC) must lie on the perpendicular bisector of AC.

Hence, the interior point O must exclusively lie on the diagonal segment BD.

This makes D, O, and B collinear, forming a straight angle ∠DOB = 180º.

Required value = ⁵/₉ × 180º = 100º.

**∴ The correct answer is 100º.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

ABCD is a rhombus.

O is an interior point such that OA = OC.

**Formula Used:**

The locus of all points equidistant from two points A and C is the perpendicular bisector of the line segment AC.

 
 

 
 
 
• 
 
• 
 
 
 
• 
 
• 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 A
 C
 B
 D
 O
 
 
 

 
 
 
• 
 
• 

**Calculations:**

⇒ In rhombus ABCD, the diagonal BD functions strictly as the perpendicular bisector of the diagonal AC.

⇒ Because OA = OC, the interior point O is geometrically bounded to lie on this specific perpendicular bisector.

⇒ Consequently, O must lie on the interior line segment connecting points B and D.

⇒ With O positioned directly between B and D, the points D, O, and B become entirely collinear.

⇒ A collinear line visually forms a completely straight angle, meaning ∠DOB = 180º.

⇒ Required measure = ⁵/₉ × ∠DOB

⇒ Required measure = ⁵/₉ × 180º = 100º

**∴ The correct answer is 100º.**

**__Additional Information__**

Properties of a Rhombus

A rhombus is a type of quadrilateral where all four sides possess an equal length. Its unique diagonal property dictates that diagonals perpendicularly bisect each other at a 90º intersection while also actively bisecting opposite interior angles.

Locus of Equidistant Points

Any generic point mapping an identical and equal distance dynamically relative to two fixed stationary points A and B will fundamentally form an invisible tracing line representing their shared perpendicular bisector.

Straight Angle

questions.question: ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral such that when sides AB and DC are produced, they meet at E, and sides AD and BC meet at F, when produced. If ∠ADE = 80° and ∠AED = 50°, then what is the measure of ∠AFB?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

∠ADE = 80° 

∠AED = 50° 

**Concept used:**

In a cyclic quadrilateral, the sum of opposite angles are 180° 

Sum of linear pair of angles of is always 180° 

Sum of all 3 interior angles of triangle is 180° 

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7f2241474a43ab8cd86e7b7125fbfecb8c9e9a150fc9c78c7322e9307e317f05.png] 

∠ADE + ∠ABC = 180° 

⇒ 80° + ∠ABC = 180° 

⇒ ∠ABC = (180° – 80°)

⇒ ∠ABC = 100° 

∠ABC + ∠CBE = 180° [straight line]

⇒ 100° + ∠CBE = 180° 

⇒ ∠CBE = (180° – 100°)

⇒ ∠CBE = 80° 

In ΔAED

⇒ ∠AED + ∠CBE + ∠ECB = 180° 

⇒ 50° + 80° + ∠ECB = 180° 

⇒ 130° + ∠ECB = 180° 

⇒ ∠ECB = (180° – 130°)

⇒ ∠ECB = 50° 

 Now,

⇒ ∠ECB = ∠DCF = 50° (Vertically opposite angles)

and 

∠FDC = 180° - ∠ADC (Linear pair)

∠FDC = 180° - 80° = 100°

∠FDC + ∠DCF + ∠AFB = 180° 

⇒ 100° + 50° + ∠AFB = 180° 

⇒ 150° + ∠AFB = 180° 

⇒ ∠AFB = (180° – 150°)

⇒ ∠AFB = 30° 

**∴ The required value of ∠AFB is 30° **

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7f2241474a43ab8cd86e7b7125fbfecb8c9e9a150fc9c78c7322e9307e317f05.png] 

From the above diagram,

⇒ ∠ADC + ∠CDF = 180° [ Linear pair of angles]

⇒ 80° + ∠CDF = 180° 

⇒ ∠CDF = 100° 

Now, In ΔAED

⇒ ∠AED + ∠ADE + ∠EAD = 180° 

⇒ 50° + 80° + ∠EAD = 180° 

⇒ ∠EAD = 180° - 130° = 50° 

Now, ∠EAD = ∠DCF = 50° 

In ΔDCF

⇒ ∠CDF + ∠DFC + ∠DCF = 180° 

⇒ 100° + ∠DFC + 50° = 180° 

⇒ ∠DFC = 180° - 150° = 30° 

⇒ ∠DFC = ∠AFB = 30° 

∴ The required value of ∠AFB is 30°

questions.question: The area of quadrilateral is 336 cm² and the perpendiculars drawn to one diagonal from the opposite vertices are 16 cm and 12 cm long. Find the length of this diagonal.
questions.solution:
**GIVEN:**

Area of quadrilateral = 336 

Perpendiculars to one diagonal from the opposite vertices (CF) = 16 and AE =12 respectively.

**FORMULA USED:**

Area of quadrilateral = 1/2 × diagonal × [sum of perpendiculars on diagonal form opposite vertices].

**CALCULATION:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c64e06229e71767f9f5ffa49961ede29bcdf37531396df70803999de702f958d.png] 

Area = 1/2 × diagonal × [CF + AE]

⇒ 336 = 1/2 × diagonal × [16 + 12]

⇒ 336 = 1/2 × diagonal × 28 

Diagonal = 336/14 = 24 cm.

**∴ The required length of the diagonal is 24 cm.**

questions.question: A cyclic quadrilateral ABCD is drawn in a circle with center O. A and C are joined O. If ∠ABC = 2p and ∠ADC = 3p, what is the measure (in degrees) of the ∠AOC reflex?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

∠ABC = 2p and ∠ADC = 3p

**Concept used:**

The reflex angle is more than 180° but less than 360°

The sum of the opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral is 180°

The angle at the center of a circle is twice the angle at the circumference of the circle.

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/795646e00334bce07a5bfc6e486643bdfa4dd9ed73e1df9d2a43a63ea4c498a5.png] 

∠ABC + ∠ADC = 180°

⇒ 2p + 3p = 180°

⇒ 5p = 180°

⇒ p = 180°/5 = 36°

So, ∠ABC = 2 × 36° = 72° and ∠ADC = 3 × 36° = 108°

Then ∠AOC = 2 × 72° = 144° [∵ ∠ABC = 72°] (Concept used)

Another side of ∠AOC =360° - 144° = 216°

**∴ The measure (in degrees) of the ∠AOC reflex is 216°**

questions.question: WXYZ is a quadrilateral in which XQ and ZP are perpendicular to WY such that XQ = ZP. Diagonals ZX and WY intersect each other at point O. If OX = 12 cm, then find the value of ZX (in cm).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When perpendiculars drawn from opposite vertices of a quadrilateral to a diagonal are equal, that diagonal bisects the other diagonal.

Therefore, diagonal WY bisects diagonal ZX at intersection point O.

This directly means OX = OZ.

Given OX = 12 cm, the full length is ZX = 2 × OX.

⇒ ZX = 2 × 12 = 24 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 24 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 
• 
• 
• 
• 
 
 
• 
• W Y X Z Q P O 12 cm 

**Given:**

⇒ WXYZ is a quadrilateral with diagonal WY.

⇒ XQ ⊥ WY and ZP ⊥ WY.

⇒ XQ = ZP

⇒ OX = 12 cm

**Method Used:**

In ▵OXQ and ▵OZP:

⇒ ∠XQO = ∠ZPO = 90° (Given perpendiculars)

⇒ ∠XOQ = ∠ZOP (Vertically opposite angles are equal)

⇒ XQ = ZP (Given equal lengths)

⇒ ∴ ▵OXQ ≅ ▵OZP (By AAS congruence criterion)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Since ▵OXQ ≅ ▵OZP, their corresponding parts are equal.

⇒ OX = OZ (By CPCT - Corresponding Parts of Congruent Triangles)

⇒ Since OX = 12 cm, we have OZ = 12 cm.

⇒ The total length of diagonal ZX = OX + OZ

⇒ ZX = 12 + 12 = 24 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 24 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

AAS Congruence Rule

If any two angles and a non-included side of one triangle are equal to the corresponding angles and side of another triangle, the two triangles are congruent.

Area of Quadrilateral Property

If perpendiculars drawn from opposite vertices to a diagonal are equal in length, the diagonal divides the entire quadrilateral into two regions of exactly equal area.

Properties of Diagonals

Whenever a diagonal line of a quadrilateral divides the other diagonal into two equal halves, it must pass strictly through the midpoint of that second diagonal.

questions.question: The parallel sides of a trapezium are 30 cm and 20 cm and its non-parallel sides are both equal. If the area of the trapezium is 300 cm², then what is the length (in cm) of each non-parallel side?

**Given:**

The parallel sides of a trapezium are 30 cm and 20 cm

The trapezium has two equal heights which are AE = DF = 12 cm

Now, Triangle DFC is a right angle triangle

Using Pythagoras theorem 

DC² = FC² + DF²

DC² = 5² + 12²

DC² = 169

DC = √169

DC = 13 cm

Length of each of two non parallel sides AB = CD = 13 cm.

questions.question: The length and the breadth of the floor of a rectangular hall are 126 feet and 90 feet, respectively. What will be the area (in square feet) of each of the largest identical square tiles that can be used to tile this floor in a way that no part of the floor remains uncovered?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Length = 126 feet

Breadth = 90 feet

**Calculation:**

To find the largest square tile size, We have to find the Greatest Common Divisor (GCD) of 126 and 90.

GCD(126, 90):

126 = 2 × 63 = 2 × 3 × 21 = 2 × 3 × 3 × 7

90 = 2 × 45 = 2 × 3 × 15 = 2 × 3 × 3 × 5

Common factors are 2 × 3 × 3 = 18.

So, the largest size of the square tile is 18 feet by 18 feet.

The area of each tile = 18 × 18 = 324 square feet.

**∴ Option 3 is the correct answer.**

⇒ ∠DBC = (3x+2)º

**Method:**

Since the adjacent sides are equal, ABCD is a kite. The diagonal BD divides the kite into two congruent triangles, ΔABD and ΔCBD.

In ΔABD and ΔCBD:

⇒ AB = CB (Given)

⇒ AD = CD (Given)

⇒ BD = BD (Common Side)

⇒ By SSS congruence criterion, ΔABD ≅ ΔCBD.

Corresponding angles of congruent triangles are equal (CPCT):

⇒ ∠ABD = ∠CBD

⇒ 68 = 3x + 2

⇒ 3x = 66 ⇒ x = 22

Also,

⇒ ∠ADB = ∠CDB

⇒ 2y − 7 = 33

⇒ 2y = 40 ⇒ y = 20

Now, calculate the value of 2x + 3y:

⇒ 2x + 3y = 2 × 22 + 3 × 20

⇒ 44 + 60 = 104

**∴ The correct answer is 104.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of a Kite

A kite is a quadrilateral with two distinct pairs of equal-length sides that are adjacent to each other. Its diagonals intersect at right angles (90º).

Congruence in Kite

The main diagonal (connecting the vertices where the equal sides meet) divides the kite into two congruent triangles via the SSS rule.

Area of a Kite

The area of a kite is half the product of the lengths of its diagonals: Area = ½ × d₁ × d₂.

questions.question: If the area of a regular pentagon is 3920 sqrt{3} cm², then how long is its each side?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Area of a regular pentagon = 3920 √(3) cm²

**Formula used:**

Area of a regular pentagon = (5/4) × a² × cot(π/5)

Where, a = side length

**Calculation:**

3920 √(3) = (5/4) × a² × cot(π/5)

⇒ a² = (3920 √(3) × 4) / (5 × cot(π/5))

cot(π/5) = √(5 + 2√5)

⇒ a² = (3920 √(3) × 4) / (5 × √(5 + 2√5))

⇒ a² = 15680 √(3) / (5 × √(5 + 2√5))

⇒ a² ≈ 3136

⇒ a ≈ √3136

⇒ a ≈ 56 cm

**∴ The correct answer is option (2).**

questions.question: ABCD is cyclic quadrilateral. Sides AB and DC, when produced, meet at E, and sides BC and AD, when produced, meet at F. If ∠BFA = 60° and ∠AED = 30°, then the measure of ∠ABC is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

ABCD is cyclic quadrilateral. 

∠BFA = 60° and ∠AED = 30°

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/14e4a3115001bdf4f2ebcf825d35ff81dd61d89fd3d83d546a1cc526c788aa4e.png] 

∠BFA = 60 & ∠BED = 30

Let ∠ABC = θ

∵ ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral

∴ ∠ADC + ∠ABC = 180

∠ADC = 180 – θ ---- (1)

Now,

∠ADC + ∠FDC = 180 [straight line]

From Equation (1);

180 – θ + ∠FDC = 180

∠FDC = θ

In ΔDFC

∠FDC + ∠DFC + FCD = 180

θ + 60 + ∠FCD = 180

∠FCD = 180 – 60 – θ = 120 – θ

∠FCD = ∠BCE = (120 – θ) [Vertical opposite angle]

∠ABC + ∠CBE = 180 [straight line]

∠CBE = 180 – θ

In ΔBEC

∠CBE + ∠BCE + ∠BEC = 180

180 – θ + 120 – θ + 30 = 180

2θ = 330 – 180 = 150

θ = 150/2 = 75

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/11f5e14389b0056864ff334b21f84fdd3d90b6d2018e4a55880024f899e6d232.png] 

In triangle ABF

α + θ + 60 = 180 

⇒ α + θ = 120 → (1)

In triangle ADE

α + π - θ + 30 = 180

⇒ α - θ + 30 = 0 → (2)

From Eqⁿ (1) and (2), we have

α = 45° and θ = 75°

∴ ∠ABC = 75°

questions.question:
In the following figure, if angles ∠ABC = 95∘ ∠FED = 115∘ (not to scale). Then the angle ∠APC is equal to?:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f0f9a8f57bf09cf40630e51448f5d74d2b1947b20ed83a11af641830776565a8.png]
questions.solution:
**Given:**

∠ABC = 95° and ∠FED = 115°

**Formula:**

The sum of the opposite angle of cycle quadrilateral is 180°.

**Calculation:**

Join A to F

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca716b55ad4509b43978f9fed33271a79528887328d616ebf066cb6b658a6866.png] 

In quadrilateral ABCF

∠ABC + ∠AFC = 180

⇒ 95 + ∠AFC = 180

⇒ ∠AFC = 180 - 95

⇒ ∠AFC = 85

In quadrilateral AFED

∠FAD + ∠FED = 180

⇒ ∠FAD + 115 = 180

⇒ ∠FAD = 180 - 115

⇒ ∠FAD = 65

In ΔAFP

⇒ ∠AFP + ∠FAP + ∠FPA = 180

⇒ 85 + 65 + ∠FPA = 180

⇒ ∠FPA = 180 - 150

⇒ ∠FPA = 30

∠APC + ∠FPA = 180 (linear pair)

⇒ ∠APC + 30 = 180

⇒ ∠APC = 180 - 30

∴ ∠APC = 150
